issues.explanation: The fairness history only counts tickets whose current status is `called`. Once tickets can move to later statuses (served, skipped), recent calls would drop out of the last-three window; `whereNotNull('called_at')` alone matches the rule as written.

When fairness restricts the call to normals and the only waiting normal is called concurrently via Ticket::call() between the fairness check and the candidate lock, the action throws NoWaitingTicketsException even though priority tickets are still waiting, instead of falling back to priority.
Every eligible waiting ticket is loaded into memory to call one; for long queues, fetch lazily or in small batches.

review.summary: Implements CallNextTicket with the CallMode enum, NoWaitingTicketsException, a queue-row lock with inactive rejection, deterministic ordering, the fairness rule limited to Any mode and a candidate re-lock and re-check. It comes with thorough Pest tests, including stale-model and concurrent-call cases, and updates the docs and CHANGELOG. It is close to approvable; the only gaps are small edge cases: the fairness history filters on the current `called` status, and a concurrent call can leave the fairness restriction with no candidate.
